latest_release.name: v0.49.0
latest_release.body:
# Atlantis v0.49.0

v0.49.0 is a **breaking release**, for three reasons:

1. **The Docker images no longer include Terraform or OpenTofu.** This was announced in v0.48.0.
2. **12 security advisories are fixed here,** and several of those fixes change behavior that existing setups may rely on.
3. **v0.47.1 shipped a breaking change without saying so:** the shell-injection fix in #6792. It is listed below so anyone upgrading from v0.47.0 or earlier sees it.

Every behavior change is also documented, in a **Behavior change** note, on the docs page where you would look for that setting. Read **Breaking changes** before you upgrade.

## Upgrade checklist

- [ ] **Docker images:** set `--default-tf-version` (and `--default-tf-distribution opentofu` if you use OpenTofu) so Atlantis downloads the binary. If downloads are blocked, mount or copy a binary into the image instead. The image no longer ships one.
- [ ] **Upgrading from v0.47.0 or earlier:** check workspace names and comment arguments against the v0.47.1 changes below.
- [ ] **GitHub / GHES:** make sure `--gh-hostname` matches the host in your repositories' clone URLs. Webhooks whose clone URL is on a different host are now rejected.
- [ ] **Server-side repo config:** if repos use `allow_custom_workflows: true` together with `allowed_workflows`, check that every project's `workflow` is in the allow-list. Repo configs that used to pass can now be rejected.
- [ ] **Project dirs:** make sure no project `dir` is a symlink to somewhere outside the repository.
- [ ] **Comment commands:** tell users that `-out`, `-generate-config-out`, `-state`, `-state-out` and `-backup` are now blocked after `--`, and that `--blocked-extra-args` can no longer unblock anything.
- [ ] **Comment `-var-file`:** the allowlist now applies to `apply`, `import` and `state rm` as well as `plan`. Paths containing `..` are refused, and so are repo symlinks that point outside the repository and the allowlist.
- [ ] **`state rm`:** if `state` is in `--allow-commands`, `state rm` now has to meet the project's `apply_requirements` and `import_requirements`.
- [ ] **API:** if `--api-secret` is set, send `X-Atlantis-Token` on `GET /api/locks`. Check that `/api/plan` and `/api/apply` callers send clean, repo-relative `paths[].directory` values with no leading `/` and no globs.
- [ ] **Approvals (GitHub, Gitea):** `apply_requirements: [approved]` now uses each reviewer's latest review. On Gitea, dismissed and stale approvals no longer count, and any push that changes the diff makes approvals stale.
- [ ] **Apply:** plans recorded by v0.49.0 are bound to a hash. A plan file that changes between `plan` and `apply` is rejected and has to be re-planned.

## Breaking changes

### Docker images

**The Docker images no longer include Terraform or OpenTofu**

- **What changed:** the `latest`, `vX.Y.Z` and `vX.Y.Z-debian` images no longer bundle Terraform or OpenTofu binaries, and they set no default Terraform version. This was announced in the v0.48.0 release notes. The `-alpine-slim` and `-debian-slim` images from v0.48.0 were the intermediate step toward this and are **no longer published**. If you pinned one, switch to the unsuffixed, `-alpine` or `-debian` tag, which now contain the same thing. If you build the image yourself, use `--target alpine` or `--target debian`; the `-slim` targets are gone.
- **Why:** every advisory against any bundled Terraform or OpenTofu release showed up in scans of the Atlantis image, whether or not you used that version. Atlantis can't own the security lifecycle of those third-party binaries.
- **Who is affected:** anyone using the published images who relied on the bundled `terraform` or `tofu` binary on `PATH`, or on the version the image used to set by default.
- **How to tell:** the server refuses to start with `terraform not found in $PATH. Set --default-tf-version ...`.
- **What to do:**
  - Set `--default-tf-version` (`ATLANTIS_DEFAULT_TF_VERSION

# Atlantis [![Latest Release](https://img.shields.io/github/release/runatlantis/atlantis.svg)](https://github.com/runatlantis/atlantis/releases/latest) [![SuperDopeBadge](./runatlantis.io/public/hightower-super-dope.svg)](https://twitter.com/kelseyhightower/status/893260922222813184) [![Go Report Card](https://goreportcard.com/badge/github.com/runatlantis/atlantis)](https://goreportcard.com/report/github.com/runatlantis/atlantis) [![Go Reference](https://pkg.go.dev/badge/github.com/runatlantis/atlantis.svg)](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/runatlantis/atlantis) [![Slack](https://img.shields.io/badge/Join-Atlantis%20Community%20Slack-red)](https://slack.cncf.io/) [![OpenSSF Scorecard](https://api.scorecard.dev/projects/github.com/runatlantis/atlantis/badge)](https://scorecard.dev/viewer/?uri=github.com/runatlantis/atlantis) [![OpenSSF Best Practices](https://www.bestpractices.dev/projects/9428/badge)](https://www.bestpractices.dev/projects/9428)



Terraform Pull Request Automation

- [Get involved](#get-involved) - [Resources](#resources) - [What is Atlantis?](#what-is-atlantis) - [What does it do?](#what-does-it-do) - [Why should you use it?](#why-should-you-use-it) - [Stargazers over time](#stargazers-over-time) ## Get involved Help shape Atlantis! Share feedback, discuss ideas, report issues, or contribute code and documentation. - **Community meetings:** Join the conversation at an [Atlantis community meeting](https://zoom-lfx.platform.linuxfoundation.org/meetings/atlantis). - **Slack:** Join [CNCF Slack](https://slack.cncf.io/) and find **#atlantis** for questions and feedback, or **#atlantis-contributors** to discuss ideas and contributions. - **Issues:** [Report a bug or suggest an improvement](https://github.com/runatlantis/atlantis/issues). - **Contributing:** See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) to get started. ## Resources * How to get started: [www.runatlantis.io/guide](https://www.runatlantis.io/guide) * Full documentation: [www.runatlantis.io/docs](https://www.runatlantis.io/docs) * Download the latest release: [github.com/runatlantis/atlantis/releases/latest](https://github.com/runatlantis/atlantis/releases/latest) ## What is Atlantis? A self-hosted golang application that listens for Terraform pull request events via webhooks. ## What does it do? Runs `terraform plan`, `import`, `apply` remotely and comments back on the pull request with the output. ## Why should you use it? * Make Terraform changes visible to your whole team. * Enable non-operations engineers to collaborate on Terraform. * Standardize your Terraform workflows. ## Stargazers over time [![Stargazers over time](https://starchart.cc/runatlantis/atlantis.svg)](https://starchart.cc/runatlantis/atlantis)
